Analytic replay: project the parameter sphere along p_3, maximize the quadratic at the interval endpoints, and check the closed profile by differentiation or the first four sine-power integrals. The sharper local expansion is I(r)=r^5/20+r^7/280+O(r^9).
correctness.rationale: Use right unit-quaternion multiplication to make the first vector coordinate u real and nonnegative (the zero case is allowed). For the other coordinate q, put t=u^2-|q|^2 and p=2u q in real coordinates; the whole sphere t^2+|p|^2=1 is attained, including t=-1. The Hermitian off-diagonal part contributes x=2cu Re(jq)=-cp_2. The i coefficient of conjugate(q) i q is 2(q_0^2+q_1^2)-|q|^2, giving |v|^2=(d+st)^2/4+ab(p_0^2+p_1^2). Since p_3 is invisible, its square fills any sphere slack: at fixed x the feasible (t,p_0,p_1) form the closed radius-R ball with R=sqrt(1-x^2/c^2). Its connected image gives an interval. Minimizing takes p_0=p_1=0 and clips the lower endpoint at zero; maximizing takes p_0^2+p_1^2=R^2-t^2 and then t=R by convexity of the resulting quadratic and d>=0. The endpoints are L=max(0,d-sR)/2 and U=(d+sR)/2, valid also at x=±c and d=0. Quaternionic conjugation fills all imaginary directions. Concavity of U and the convex hull of each outer sphere establish the proposed convex hull. The missing section has volume 4 pi L^3/3; symmetry, the factor 1/8 from cubing L and x=c cos(theta) give the prefactor pi c s^3/3. The stated elementary antiderivative expression vanishes at zero and its derivative 3r^2+2-(r^2+2)sqrt(1-r^2)-3r arcsin(r) equals the differentiated integral. Rescaling sin(theta)=rt gives I(r)=r^5(1/20+O(r^2)); the positive integral and its monotone integrand verify strict increase of the normalized profile and the sharp coefficient pi c/(60 s^2) multiplying d^5. The zero deficit occurs exactly at d=0.
residual_risks: Direct numerical evaluation of the elementary closed form near r=0 loses precision by cancellation; use the positive rescaled integral or the expansion there. The proof concerns the given parameter domain, not arbitrary quaternionic matrices.
